summary: With only a same-category oracle, an all-distinct input requires querying every unordered pair because any unqueried pair could instead form one category without contradicting observed answers; the accepted pair scan matches this quadratic lower bound.

optimality.argument: On the all-distinct transcript every query returns false. For any unqueried pair, changing only those two elements to share a category preserves every observed answer but changes the correct count from n to n-1, so all n(n-1)/2 pairs are necessary. The accepted scan asks each unordered pair at most once.

replacement_checks.evidence: An indistinguishability adversary on the all-distinct transcript forces all n(n-1)/2 pair queries.
For index i, the reference asks at most i earlier indices and therefore makes at most n(n-1)/2 calls using constant auxiliary state.
Cases cover one element, adjacent and interleaved categories, a late repeat, and n = 100 with both all-distinct and all-equal assignments.
